explanation: A Canadian veterinary officer, Harry Colebourn, bought the black bear cub in Ontario in 1914 and named her after Winnipeg. Christopher Robin Milne often visited her.

claims.text: Winnie-the-Pooh was named partly after Winnie, a Canadian black bear at London Zoo.
Winnie the bear did not come from Russia, Finland or India.
Harry Colebourn, a Canadian army veterinary officer, bought the bear cub in Ontario in 1914.
Colebourn named the bear Winnie after the city of Winnipeg.
A. A. Milne's son, Christopher Robin Milne, often visited Winnie at London Zoo.
